data.name: 7 Days to Die
data.detailed_description:
HOW LONG WILL YOU SURVIVE?

With over 20 million copies sold, 7 Days has defined the survival genre, with unrivaled crafting and world-building content. Set in a brutally unforgiving post-apocalyptic world overrun by the undead, 7 Days is an open-world game that is a unique combination of first-person shooter, survival horror, tower defense, and role-playing games. It presents combat, crafting, looting, mining, exploration, and character growth, in a way that has seen a rapturous response from fans worldwide. Play the definitive zombie survival sandbox RPG that came first. Navezgane awaits!

GAME FEATURES

  • Explore - Huge, unique and rich environments, offering the freedom to play the game any way you want, featuring 5 unique biomes and worlds up to 100 square kilometers in size.

  • Craft – Handcraft and repair weapons, clothes, armor, tools, vehicles, and more with over 500 recipes. Learn more powerful recipes by finding schematics.

  • Build – Design your fort to include traps, electric power, auto turrets, automated doors, gadgets and defensive positions to survive the undead in a fully destructible and moldable world.

  • Cooperate or Compete – Work together to build settlements or against each other raiding other player’s bases, it’s really up to you in a wasteland where zombies and outlaws rule the land.

  • Create – Unleash your creativity with access to over 800 in-game items, and over 1,300 unique building blocks and a painting system that offers infinite possibilities.

  • Improve – Increase your skills with a multitude of perks under 5 main attributes. Gain additional skills by reading over 100 books. 7 Days to Die is the only true survival RPG.

  • Choose – Play the campaign world, or dive back in a randomly-generated world with cities, towns, lakes, mountains, valleys, roads, caves and over 700 unique locations.

  • Combat – Encounter nearly 60 unique zombie archetypes including special infected with unique behaviors and attacks progressing in difficulty to provide an infinite challenge.

  • Survive – Experience real hardcore survival mechanics with nearly 50 buffs, boosts and ailments that will impact the gameplay in ways that can both challenge and aid in your survival.

  • Destroy – Buildings and terrain formations can collapse under their own weight from structural damage or poor building design with real structural stability.

  • Loot – Scavenge the world for the best weapons, tools, and armor with 6 quality ranges providing thousands of permutations. Augment items with a multitude of mods.

  • Quest – Meet several Trader NPCs who buy and sell goods and offer quest jobs for rewards. Enjoy many unique quest types supported by over 700 locations.

  • Customize – Create your own character and customize your character further in-game with a huge selection of clothing and armor you can craft or loot in the world.

  • Drive – Enjoy the badass vehicle system where you find all the parts, learn the recipes, craft and customize your own bicycle, minibike, motorcycle, 4x4 or gyrocopters and ride with friends.

  • Farm or Hunt – Plant and grow gardens for sustainable resources or head out into the wilderness and hunt over a dozen unique wild animals.

reviews.review:
[h1]DEVS, WAKE UP! NEW PLAYERS, DON'T BE FOOLED! WE DESERVE BETTER![/h1]

I've been playing 7 Days to Die since Alpha 16. Steam shows over 700 hours, but my actual playtime is probably closer to 1,500+ hours, including hundreds of hours with overhaul mods like Dead Legacy.

I LOVE this game. And that is exactly why I'm so frustrated with what The Fun Pimps have been doing.

Before anyone says "you're just nostalgic, old versions weren't better" — [b]NO. THAT IS NOT THE POINT.[/b]

My problem isn't that the game has changed. My problem is the endless cycle of [b]REMOVING features, bringing them back YEARS later, presenting them as major updates, and repeatedly delaying genuinely promised content.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]LET'S TALK ABOUT THE HISTORY THAT NEW PLAYERS DON'T KNOW.[/h2]

Remember Alpha 16?

We had deeper skill progression, meaningful crafting, detailed clothing and temperature mechanics, and the ability to combine equipment to improve its quality. Exploration was exciting because you could actually get lucky and find powerful equipment early.

Then came Alpha 17 and the versions that followed.

Skill systems were replaced. Item combining disappeared. Survival mechanics were repeatedly simplified or redesigned. The old clothing system was eventually removed. Loot progression became increasingly restricted by artificial game stages.

I could accept these changes if they consistently led to something better. Not every old mechanic was perfect.

But here's where things become ridiculous.

[h3]LOOK AT WHAT IS NOW BEING PRESENTED AS MAJOR FEATURES:[/h3]

[list]
[*][b]SMELL SYSTEM![/b] We had this years ago. It was removed. Now it returns as a major survival feature.
[*][b]TEMPERATURE AND CLOTHING![/b] Heat, cold, wetness, and clothing-based protection existed in the old alphas. After years of redesigns, we are celebrating their return.
[*][b]ITEM COMBINING![/b] This existed in Alpha 15–16, disappeared in Alpha 17, and returned in version 3.0 as the Combine Station.
[*][b]EMPTY JARS![/b] Even basic reusable containers were removed, only to return years later.
[/list]

Yes, the new implementations aren't always identical. And yes, there have been some genuinely new additions.

[b]BUT WHY SHOULD WE CELEBRATE GETTING BACK FEATURES WE ALREADY HAD YEARS AGO AS IF THEY WERE GROUNDBREAKING INNOVATIONS?[/b]

Imagine buying a car. The manufacturer removes its air conditioning, heated seats, and navigation system.

Years later, they proudly announce major upgrades:

[i]"Air conditioning is back!"[/i]

[i]"Heated seats are back!"[/i]

Would you call that innovation?

[hr][/hr]

[h2]AND NOW, LET'S TALK ABOUT THE BIGGEST JOKE OF ALL: BANDITS.[/h2]

New players might think bandits are some exciting new feature currently being developed.

[b]VETERAN PLAYERS KNOW BETTER.[/b]

Bandits have been part of this game's plans since its earliest days.

They were mentioned in the original 2013 Kickstarter vision.

In 2015, the developers were already recording voice work intended for future bandits.

In the official Alpha 15 release notes back in 2016, they explicitly stated that the NPC system would be used for bandits in upcoming updates.

[b]2016! TEN YEARS AGO![/b]

And the story doesn't end there.

For years, we watched developer streams, read announcements, and heard about the future of bandits, factions, and the game's storyline.

In 2023, the official developer diary listed bandits FIRST in its "Roadmap to Gold and Beyond" and stated that they should be ready for Alpha 22.

Remember what happened to Alpha 22?

[b]IT BECAME VERSION 1.0.[/b]

But the bandits weren't there.

Instead, the developers announced that the game was leaving Early Access, despite major planned systems still being unfinished.

And here's the incredible part: in their own 2024 FAQ, they acknowledged that some systems weren't ready and explained that they had decided to release 1.0 rather than continue with more alpha versions.

The price increased from $24.99 to $44.99.

Bandits were moved to the post-launch roadmap, initially targeting Q2 2025.

[b]IT IS NOW OCTOBER 2026.[/b]

[b]WHERE. ARE. THE. BANDITS?[/b]

After all these years of promises, previews, development discussions, and missed targets, how much longer are we supposed to wait?

I understand that development is difficult. I understand that AI systems are complicated. I understand that plans change.

But we're not talking about a six-month delay.

[b]WE ARE TALKING ABOUT A FEATURE THAT HAS BEEN DISCUSSED FOR MORE THAN A DECADE.[/b]

And the same goes for the long-awaited story and faction systems.

What exactly was the point of calling the game 1.0 if so many fundamental parts of its original vision were still missing?

From my perspective, this was a marketing milestone, not the completion of the game we had been waiting for.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]NEW PLAYERS DON'T KNOW THE HISTORY. AND THAT'S THE PROBLEM.[/h2]

A new player sees an update announcement:

[i]"New smell system!"[/i]

[i]"Improved temperature survival!"[/i]

[i]"Combine your weapons!"[/i]

And naturally thinks:

[i]"Wow, these developers keep adding so much content!"[/i]

But veteran players remember when much of this already existed.

I'm not saying the developers have literally done nothing. They've improved graphics, added locations, reworked systems, and implemented genuinely new features.

[b]BUT RESTORING PREVIOUSLY REMOVED FUNCTIONALITY IS NOT THE SAME AS DELIVERING NEW CONTENT.[/b]

Especially when major features advertised and discussed for YEARS remain unfinished.

And what makes the situation even worse?

[b]7 DAYS TO DIE IS STILL AN INCREDIBLY UNIQUE GAME.[/b]

There are very few alternatives that combine voxel destruction, base building, survival, exploration, and zombie hordes this well.

That's why I keep coming back.

That's why I've spent well over a thousand hours playing it.

And that's why this situation makes me so angry.

The game's uniqueness has allowed the developers to get away with decisions that would have driven players away from many other games.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]TO THE FUN PIMPS:[/h2]

You created something special. You have a community that has supported this project for over a decade.

We don't expect miracles.

[b]We expect transparency, meaningful progress, and the delivery of long-promised features.[/b]

Stop treating the return of old mechanics as a substitute for actual innovation.

Stop moving major features further and further into the future without clear accountability.

You have an amazing foundation. PLEASE FINISH BUILDING ON IT.

[h2]TO NEW PLAYERS:[/h2]

Enjoy the game. It genuinely has a lot to offer.

But understand that many of the features now being celebrated as major updates existed in some form years ago.

And many of the features we've been waiting for still haven't arrived.

[h2]TO VETERAN PLAYERS:[/h2]

[b]IF YOU SHARE THESE FRUSTRATIONS, PLEASE DON'T STAY SILENT.[/b]

Leave an honest review. Explain what was removed, what was promised, and what you're still waiting for.

If your experience justifies a negative review, don't be afraid to leave one.

Let the developers see that longtime players are paying attention.

We have supported this game with our money, our time, and our loyalty for YEARS.

[hr][/hr]

[h1]WE ARE NOT ASKING FOR THE OLD GAME BACK.[/h1]

[h2]WE ARE ASKING FOR REAL PROGRESS, HONEST COMMUNICATION, AND DELIVERED PROMISES.[/h2]

[b]DEVELOPERS, WAKE UP. YOUR COMMUNITY DESERVES BETTER![/b]
